Self-supervised representation audit: SimCLR on industrial castings¶

CST 620, Week 3. Can SimCLR pretraining replace expensive manual labels for defect inspection? Data: Kaggle casting product images (casting_512x512, 1,300 un-augmented originals), standing in for wafer inspection.

This notebook only reads results/ and weights/. It trains nothing and scores nothing; every number was produced by the pipeline (data.py, check_splits.py, train_ssl.py, baselines.py, eval.py, contaminated.py). Test was scored exactly once (results/eval.lock).

In [1]:
import json
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, Markdown, display

R, W = Path("results"), Path("weights")          # the only folders this notebook reads
pd.set_option("display.precision", 3)

def load(name):
    """Read a JSON file from results/."""
    return json.loads((R / name).read_text())

def show(name, width=900):
    """Display a PNG from results/."""
    display(Image(filename=str(R / name), width=width))

def ms(s):
    """mean +/- sample std over draws (a single draw prints the value only)."""
    return f"{s.mean():.3f}" if len(s) < 2 else f"{s.mean():.3f} +/- {s.std(ddof=1):.3f}"

lock = load("eval.lock")
manifest = load("frozen_manifest.json")
checked = {k: v for k, v in manifest["files"].items() if v["path"].replace("\\", "/").split("/")[0] in ("weights", "results")}
ok = all(hashlib.sha256((Path(v["path"])).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == v["sha256"] for v in checked.values())
print(f"eval.lock: {lock['status']} at {lock['at_utc']} (manifest frozen {manifest['frozen_at_utc']})")
print(f"frozen weights/results files re-hashed here: {len(checked)}, all match: {ok}")

1. Data audit¶

1a. The provided train/test split leaks (casting_data/, excluded)¶

The dataset ships a 300 px set with its own train/test split. Its images are pre-augmented copies that cannot be traced to a source image, so it is excluded; audit_source.py measures how much its own split leaks.

1b. Near-duplicate grouping: three settings¶

A near-duplicate pair is the same casting photographed again; connected components become group_id, and a group never spans two splits. The 64-bit hash chains almost everything into one group. Identity-only 256-bit hashing missed 180-degree rotated and mirrored re-shots, so the final grouping takes the minimum Hamming distance over 8 orientations.

2. Augmentations¶

Castings are round and shot from the top, so views use 0-360 degree rotation, flips, brightness/contrast jitter and a random crop. The first version (crop scale 0.8-1.0, free aspect ratio, rare blur) was changed to crop scale 0.9-1.0, square crops (castings stay round) and no blur, so small pits and cracks survive every view. Rotated corners are filled with the median border pixel, not black.

In [7]:

3. SimCLR pretraining¶

ResNet-18 from scratch (weights=None), 512-d encoder, 2-layer projection head (512-512-128) used for training only, NT-Xent with cosine similarity. 96 px grayscale, CPU. The val monitor is leave-one-group-out k-NN (k=5): plain leave-one-out let rotated twins inside val vote for each other.

4. Validation selection (VAL only, not the reported result)¶

k, C, the anomaly option, thresholds, tau, and the supervised learning rate and best epoch were all chosen on the 174-image val split, so these numbers are optimistic. Label budgets per class: 10, 25, 50 (3 draws each) and all; every method at a budget uses the same labeled images.

Anomaly score (VAL)¶

Score = cosine distance of a val image to the labeled ok embeddings of the budget; the option (local k, all_ok, centroid) and the threshold (catch 95% of val defects) are chosen on val.

Grid change after seeing val¶

Anomaly grid widened AFTER seeing val: added 'all_ok' (mean cosine distance to all labeled ok embeddings) and 'centroid' (cosine distance to the labeled ok centroid). Reason, as observed on the pre_logo run: with the 'all' budget (346 ok refs), k in {1, 5, 10, 20} only measures local distance; every val image, ok or defect, has a near ok neighbor (median nearest-ok distance ratio defect/ok = 1.01), so SSL val AUROC fell to 0.57 while a global distance gave about 0.79. At 10 per class the chosen k = 10 already averaged over every ok ref, i.e. it was already a global score. Because the grid change was made after looking at val, val AUROC for the anomaly score is extra optimistic; the test run is the check.

5. Test results (scored once, frozen choices)¶

All choices were hashed into frozen_manifest.json before test was opened. The near/clean strata were computed from test images and train features before any test label was read.

7. CONTAMINATED control (leakage estimate)¶

CONTAMINATED: the SSL encoder was pretrained again with the same config on the train pool plus the 260 test images, then scored on test with the same frozen k, C, anomaly option and threshold. The gap (CONTAMINATED minus clean) estimates how much seeing test images during pretraining would inflate the SSL numbers.

8. Limitations¶

  • Small evaluation sets. Val has 174 images (one image = 0.57 points) and test 260 (0.38 points); AUROC confidence intervals are about +/- 0.13. Budget "all" is a single draw.
  • Weak pretraining by design of the compute budget. CPU only: 96 px, 10 epochs, batch 64 (126 negatives per anchor), one seed. Published SimCLR uses hundreds of epochs and thousands of negatives; this measures SimCLR under a lab-sized budget, not SimCLR at its best.
  • Val was used for many choices (tau, k, C, anomaly option, thresholds, supervised lr and epoch), and the anomaly grid was widened after seeing val. Val numbers are optimistic; only the single test run is reported.
  • Residual twins. 8-orientation hashing cannot match a casting re-shot at an arbitrary angle, so some near duplicates may still cross splits; the near/clean strata bound this effect.
  • Thresholds did not transfer. Val thresholds set for 95% defect recall missed between 0 and 16 test defects and rejected most good parts; any production threshold needs its own calibration set.
  • Supervised "all" stopped at the 20-epoch limit while still improving at lr 1e-4, so the supervised ceiling may be understated.
  • Castings stand in for wafers. Defect types, image statistics and class balance differ from semiconductor inspection.
